observation.visible_scene: A high-dynamic-range landscape of a turquoise glacial lake (Lake Louise-like) framed by forested mountains on the left and right, a snow-covered glacier in the central gap, a vivid blue sky with scattered cumulus clouds, and a band of smooth rounded rocks along the near shore. The composition, mountain silhouettes, sunlit orange patch on the left peak, and foreground rocks stay in fixed pixel positions throughout, indicating a static camera and a stable scene.
visible_changes: The central cumulus cloud mass slowly drifts and deforms over the ~1.6 s excerpt (its outline spreads and its position shifts slightly), with the small cloud near the upper-right ridge also changing shape.
The bright reflection of that central cloud on the lake surface correspondingly changes shape and position, tracking the sky cloud rather than being an independent object.
Fine ripples animate the water surface; the mirror-like reflections of the mountains and sky shimmer subtly frame to frame.
No translation, expansion, or deformation of the mountains, glacier, forest, or foreground rocks is observed; the only object motion is the cloud drift and the water-surface ripple/reflection change.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cloud drift is already underway at t=0 and continues past t=1.6 s; onset and completion are outside the crop.
The full duration and any later sky/water changes are unknown.
The reason for the HDR look and any unseen wind cause are not shown.
uncertain_details: Exact direction and speed of cloud movement (appears slow, roughly rightward/spreading, but hard to quantify).
Whether any very slight camera drift exists; background landmarks look fixed, so camera motion is treated as absent/uncertain.
Distinguishing cloud-shape evolution from HDR flicker in individual frames.
